answer: Each agent locks bonded stake and commits to a secret through a polynomial evaluated for the epoch; zero-knowledge proofs bind each message to its rate-limit nullifier without exposing that secret. A duplicate message within the epoch yields distinct Shamir shares under the same nullifier, allowing anyone to reconstruct the private key and verify the violation, so the contract can slash collateral immediately. Marble, hollow, and basalt describe no protocol components: resistance comes from verifiable commitments and enforceable stake.
